Penance in {{ls}}ackcloth.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Penance.}}By this {{ls}}ackcloth and a{{ls}}hes added here and in other places, wee {{ls}}ee euidently that Penance is not only leauing of former {{ls}}innes, and chaunge or amendement of life pa{{ls}}t, no nor bare {{ls}}orowfulnes or recounting of our offen{{ls}}es already committed, but requireth puni{{ls}}hement and cha{{ls}}ti{{ls}}emēt of our per{{ls}}ons by the{{ls}}e and {{ls}}uch other meanes as the Scriptures do els where {{ls}}et forth. and therfore concerning the worde al{{ls}}o, it is rather to be called Penance, as in our tran{{ls}}lation: then (as the Aduer{{ls}}aries of purpo{{ls}}e auoyding the word) Repentance or Amendement of life: and that according to the very v{{ls}}ual {{ls}}ignification of the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''{{lang|grc|μετάνοια}}''.}}* Greeke word in the mo{{ls}}t ancient Eccle{{ls}}ia{{ls}}tical Greeke writers: who for ''Pœnitentes'' (which in the Primitiue Churche did publike penance) {{ls}}ay, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=* ''Diony{{ls}}. Litle ones.''] The{{ls}}e litle ones doe not {{ls}}ignifie here only the vnlearned, as though Coblers and weauers and women and girles had this reuelation, and therfore do vnder{{ls}}tand al Scriptures and are able to expound them: but here are {{ls}}ignified the humble, whether they be learned or vnlearned: as when he {{ls}}ayth, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 18, 3''.}}''Vnles you become as litle ones, you {{ls}}hal not enter into the Kingdom of heauen''.
